source.title: Identifying and Manipulating Personality Traits in LLMs Through Activation Engineering
source.authors: Rumi Allbert; James K. Wiles; Vlad Grankovsky

record.tranche_reason: The study adapts difference-in-means activation directions and activation addition to manipulate personality traits, but reports no test of refusal or of the refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The study reports personality manipulation, not results on refusal, harmful-request compliance, harmless-request refusal, jailbreaks, or capability retention. Its personality prompts and example responses do not test the claim's predicted refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the difference-in-means and orthogonalization recipe from the refusal-direction paper to build personality-trait directions in an uncensored Llama 3 8B. It reports no refusal outcome, no ablation or addition of a refusal direction, and no quantitative result on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say activation engineering lets them induce and control personality traits without retraining. They also say the personality vector space shows meaningful structure (clusters and principal components, including a cluster of harmful traits), and they stress ethical safeguards. They give no quantitative evidence for the induction claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means directions and activation intervention, but targets elicited personality traits rather than harmful-versus-harmless refusal; it adds a personality direction rather than ablating the refusal direction or orthogonalizing weights.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report an effective scaling-factor range of 1.3 to 1.4; they say higher values produce garbled outputs and lower values have little effect. These are personality-method settings, not refusal results.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report qualitatively that adding a Layer-18 difference-in-means personality direction (alpha 1.3–1.4) induces personality traits; higher alpha gives garbled output. No quantitative evaluation is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means activation directions can induce personality traits in an LLM.

record.problems: The paper gives no quantitative evaluation of personality induction, no stated control comparison for that result, and no capability-retention test. The model used for the reported manipulation is not clearly identified.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for trait prompts or example responses: these illustrate prompted personalities and do not report outcomes of the activation intervention. No refusal-related rows are reported.

untested.parts: All parts: refusal direction ablation and addition, refusal rates, capability retention.
All parts: a weight-edit ablation of refusal is described as background only.
All parts. The PCA and clustering apply to personality vectors, not refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The model is described as uncensored, so refusal behaviour is not examined at all. The paper's equation 5 replaces the projection onto the direction rather than simply adding it. The record's T4 and uses_without_test classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: The refusal direction, its ablation and addition, and effects on refusal and other abilities.
Weight-edit ablation and refusal outcomes in released models.
Whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or training against ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal is represented by an affine space, cone, or multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment and refusal are separately encoded.
Transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages.
How refusal training affects whether refusal is represented by a removable direction.
Whether the claim holds for reasoning models.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Add a personality difference-in-means direction to activations; the method describes extracting activations at Layer 18.

conditions.value: 1,500 varying prompts from the Alpaca Dataset, paired with trait-specific and neutral prompts

rows.measure: Authors' qualitative report of personality induction and control
rows.value: The authors state that they demonstrated the potential for dynamic personality customization without extensive retraining.
rows.note: This is a qualitative claim about personality manipulation, not a result about refusal. The paper identifies Llama 3 8B for an activation visualization but does not clearly state the model used for this manipulation result.
rows.check: The row reports the authors' qualitative claim of personality induction, not refusal. It has no baseline, no number and no control, so 'observed' should not be read as bearing on any version. The subject is likely the uncensored Llama 3 8B named in Fig. 1, but the paper does not state this clearly for the manipulation result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
